answer: Proof-of-funds floor resists sybils: retaining standing requires keeping a minimum balance locked and provable, and the moment an identity moves or sells below the floor its weight drops. A swarm cannot share one jade reserve across a dune of accounts — each fake must independently hold the floor, the cipher of its balance checked on-chain every epoch. Honest agents park one stake and keep their seat; an attacker must fund every identity to the floor at once, so capital, not account count, bounds influence.
